findings.reason: apply.js:52-63 now breaks on the first '\' line. For `-foo`, `\ No newline`, `+bar`, `\ No newline`, only addEOFNL gets set, so lines 70-72 push '' and the result is 'bar\n', not 'bar'. When the + lines come first, only removeEOFNL gets set and line 68 returns false. The diff removed the `removeEOFNL && addEOFNL` guard that used to handle this case, and createPatch emits exactly this hunk shape.
findings.claim: The new `break` stops the scan at the first `\ No newline at end of file` marker, and the both-sides branch was deleted. A patch that changes a final line where neither version ends in a newline now adds a newline it shouldn't, or fails to apply.
findings.evidence: The loop over the last hunk's lines now `break`s after the first line starting with '\\'. In a normal unified diff the old side comes first (`-foo`, `\ No newline at end of file`, `+bar`, `\ No newline at end of file`). So the first marker follows a '-' line: only `addEOFNL = true` is set, and `removeEOFNL` stays false. Execution then reaches `else if (addEOFNL) { if (lines[lines.length - 1] != '') { lines.push(''); } ... }` (lines 70-72). Trace: source 'foo' gives lines ['foo'], then ['foo',''], and after the hunk ['bar',''], which joins to 'bar\n' instead of 'bar'. createPatch emits exactly this shape: test/patch/create.js:103-106 shows `\ No newline at end of file` / `+line44` / `\ No newline at end of file`. So a createPatch/applyPatch round trip on files without a trailing newline now gives a different file.
